dedupe_keys.name: universal digital twin integration of national scale energy systems and climate data

description: Universal Digital Twin: Integration of national-scale energy systems and climate data is a software platform described in the paper "Universal Digital Twin: Integration of national-scale energy systems and climate data" in Data-Centric Engineering (Cambridge University Press, 2022), produced by Thomas Savage, Jethro Akroyd, Sebastian Mosbach and colleagues. This article applies a knowledge graph-based approach to unify multiple heterogeneous domains inherent in climate and energy supply research. Existing approaches that rely on bespoke models with spreadsheet-type inputs are noninterpretable, static and make it difficult to combine existing domain specific models. The difficulties inherent to this approach become increasingly prevalent as energy supply models gain complexity while society pursues a net-zero future. Coverage: the United Kingdom. Access is through the paper, which is available online; the paper describes the tool and its use cases, and no separate code link was verified, so the paper is the only link. Licence: not stated (data set page not reachable on 2026-10-01; the paper is CC-BY-4.0). Cost: no charge is stated in the metadata read; the paper's own access terms were not checked. Caveats: written from the paper's abstract and metadata only, so contents, quality and current availability are unchecked and the description may lag the source. It can support linked-data modelling of the UK gas transmission system and climate data. Related: the paper is the Data-Centric Engineering article 10.1017/dce.2022.22.
